name: Superconducting Cosmic String
description: The exterior of a straight superconducting cosmic string carrying a current and surrounded by a magnetic field.
convention: We use Gaussian electromagnetic units with $c=G=1$.
history: A current along a cosmic string surrounds it with a magnetic field. The field extends beyond the core, carrying energy and stress that curve the surrounding spacetime [sen1999superconducting]. Ian Moss and Stephen Poletti found an exterior for a long, straight superconducting string in 1987, and Anjan A. Sen recovered it in 1999 [sen1999superconducting, mosspoletti1987superconducting].¶Edward Witten showed in 1985 that cosmic strings in certain gauge theories can carry superconducting currents [witten1985superconducting]. Charged bosons can condense in the string core, and charged fermions can occupy modes confined to the string [witten1985superconducting]. Arif Babul, Tsvi Piran, and David N. Spergel studied the fields and exterior geometry of an infinite bosonic superconducting string in 1988 [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical, babul1988curvature].¶The exact far exterior can be written with $x=r/\ell$ and $F=(x^m+kx^{-m})/(1+k)$, where $\ell$ is a scaling length, $k\geq 0$, and $m$ is a constant [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical]. In Gaussian electromagnetic units with $c=G=1$, its line element is $ds^2=F^2[x^{2m^2}(-dt^2+dr^2)+W^2r^2d\phi^2]+F^{-2}dz^2$, with angular scale $W>0$ [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical]. The circumference around the string is $2\pi WrF$, and the current is $I=\pm mW\sqrt{k}/(1+k)$ [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical]. The exterior electromagnetic tensor has magnetic component $F_{zr}=\pm 2m(1+k)\sqrt{k}x^{2m}/[r(x^{2m}+k)^2]$ [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical].¶Bernard Linet treated the weak field of a straight superconducting string in 1989 [dimopoulos1998magnetic, linet1989superconducting]. Restoring $G$ and keeping $c=1$, Konstantinos Dimopoulos wrote a first order exterior for a string with energy per unit length $U$, tension $T$, current $J$, and core radius $r_c$ [dimopoulos1998magnetic]. At $r>r_c$ in the weak field regime, the transverse optical deficit is $\delta=8\pi G[U+J^2(1/2+\ln(r/r_c))]$ [dimopoulos1998magnetic]. A slowly moving test particle has radial acceleration $-2G[U-T+J^2(1+2\ln(r/r_c))]/r$ at that order [dimopoulos1998magnetic].¶Sen's far exterior follows from Brans-Dicke theory when the scalar field is constant [sen1999superconducting]. Ernesto F. Eiroa and Claudio Simeone constructed cylindrical wormholes by joining two copies of this exterior at a cylindrical shell in 2004 [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical]. When $k=0$, the current and magnetic field vanish and the exterior becomes a static vacuum cylinder [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical]. Setting $m=0$ leaves a conical exterior with circumference $2\pi Wr$ [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical].

related.text: With zero current and zero cylindrical mass parameter, the exterior becomes the cone around a straight cosmic string [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical].
At $k = 0$, the exterior is a static vacuum cylinder with Weyl parameter $d = -m$ [eiroasimeone2004cylindrical].
